opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Jennifer Martin (E033) is a full-time Analyst. She requested admin to Payroll, but Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is not permitted. Maximum for full-time employees is write, so recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E033 shows contractor with basic training (note conflicts; security DB is authoritative). Contractors never get admin; with basic training max is read. Requested admin exceeds read, so recommending read.
reason: Employee E033 (Jennifer Martin) is an Analyst. Security record (authoritative per Security agent note) shows contractor employment with basic security training. Contractors never receive admin; with basic training the maximum permitted level is read. The requested admin level exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Ticket: Jennifer Martin (E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

HR agent note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Says admin not permitted because Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist role. Full-time max is write.

Security agent note: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Says security DB authoritative, contractor, basic training max read. Requested admin exceeds read, so recommending read.

There's a conflict: HR says full_time, Security says contractor (and says security DB is authoritative).

Employee is Analyst; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist role.

Access policy:
1. full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Requested: admin.

If full-time: max write (Analyst doesn't own Payroll), so grant write.
If contractor: max read (basic training), so grant read.

Which is authoritative? The Security agent says security record is authoritative on employment type and shows contractor. Hmm, but how to decide? The team says HR and Security each write notes with employee facts. Conflict resolution: Typically security DB is authoritative for employment type? The note explicitly says "note conflicts; security DB is authoritative".

So employment type = contractor, security training = basic. Then max = read. Requested admin > read, grant read.

Let me submit decision: read with reason.

But wait, is there any tool to check other info? We have the submit_decision. The available information is the notes. I should use them. The security note says security DB is authoritative, so contractor, basic training. Max read. Requested admin, grant read.

I'll submit read.
